  <h1 id="exam-title">Exam</h1>
  <p>The exam follows the spirit of the adventures: a concrete situation, a dataset, a Quarto document to complete and decisions to justify. It assesses autonomy with the essential skills from modules 1 to 4.</p>
  <div class="resource-actions" aria-label="Quick links">

  <div><span>04</span><p>Import and cleaning</p></div>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="exam-format-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="exam-format-title">General format</h2>
  <p>The exam is applied. The goal is not to recite functions, but to choose the right tools to produce a reliable short report. The individual exam is worth 25% and takes place on October 19, 2026, from 8:30 to 11:20 a.m. in PLT-2325. Authorized material, Internet access and submission instructions remain to be specified on Brio.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid">
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Narrative context</h3><p>You receive a mission or mandate, as in the course adventures.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Provided data</h3><p>You import, check, transform and summarize a dataset.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Quarto report</h3><p>Answers, code, graphs and interpretations are integrated into a reproducible document.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Interpretation</h3><p>Results must be explained briefly, carefully and in the language of the context.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="exam-ai-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="exam-ai-title">AI during the exam</h2>
  <p>AI is not allowed during the exam, as stated on Brio. During preparation, practise completing the essential tasks independently and explaining your choices. Notes and other resources used for revision are not automatically authorized during the exam; check the final Brio instructions.</p>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="exam-not-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="exam-not-title">What the exam is not</h2>
  <p>The exam is not designed to trick you or reward the most sophisticated code. It mainly checks whether you can recognize useful moves in a new situation and produce a clear trace.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Not memorization</h3><p>Questions do not ask you to reproduce a challenge word for word.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Not a speed contest</h3><p>A simple, readable and complete solution is better than an overly ambitious one.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Not only code</h3><p>Interpretations and choices must be understandable in context.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Not a team project</h3><p>The goal is to show your individual autonomy with the course foundations.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="exam-skills-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="exam-skills-title">Skills used</h2>
  <p>The tasks resemble the adventures, challenges and exercises from the first modules. The exam does not ask you to reproduce a challenge by heart; it asks you to recognize useful moves in a new situation.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">1</span><h3>Import</h3><p>Read a file, understand variables and check types.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">2</span><h3>Transform</h3><p>Filter, create variables, recode, group and summarize with <code>dplyr</code>.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">3</span><h3>Visualize</h3><p>Choose an appropriate graph and make it readable with <code>ggplot2</code>.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">4</span><h3>Explain</h3><p>Write short interpretations that answer the question.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="exam-criteria-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="exam-criteria-title">What matters</h2>
  <p>A good exam shows a complete process, even if everything is not perfect. The criteria resemble those used for challenges, but in a more integrated context.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Reproducibility</h3><p>The document renders, packages are loaded and the objects used are created in the code.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Technical choices</h3><p>Transformations are relevant to the question and basic checks are visible.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Readable graphs</h3><p>Visualizations have a clear purpose, useful titles, named axes and an understandable scale.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Careful interpretation</h3><p>Sentences answer the question without going beyond what the data support.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Organization</h3><p>The report follows a readable progression: preparation, analysis, results and conclusion.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Simplicity</h3><p>A clear solution using course tools is better than a complicated and fragile solution.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="exam-prep-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="exam-prep-title">How to prepare</h2>
  <p>During the weeks of October 5 and 12, revise modules 1 to 4 and continue exploring a dataset with your project/poster team. There is no class meeting on those Mondays. Our next meeting is the October 19 exam. The module 4 challenge is due October 4 at 11:55 p.m.; no additional project submission is added during the break.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>First, consolidate R objects, conditions, missing values, Quarto, numerical summaries, dplyr and ggplot2 using modules 1 and 2.</li>
  <li>Then revisit strings, categories, factor order, import types, duplicate rows, missing values and long/wide reshaping using modules 3 and 4.</li>
  <li>Complete an adventure or a set of exercises from a blank Quarto document without AI. Restart R and render the complete document.</li>
  <li>Explain every graph and cleaning decision in your own words. Revisit any step you cannot reproduce independently.</li>
  </ol>
  <div class="resource-link-list">
<a href="module_01/index.html"><span>Module 1</span><span>R and Quarto</span></a>
<a href="module_02/index.html"><span>Module 2</span><span>Data summaries and graphics</span></a>
<a href="module_03/index.html"><span>Module 3</span><span>Strings and categories</span></a>
<a href="module_04/index.html"><span>Module 4</span><span>Import and cleaning</span></a>
</div>
  <p>The best preparation is to redo challenges, reread the adventures and build a personal cheat sheet with your most useful examples.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>Redo the relevant module challenges without looking immediately at the solution.</li>
  <li>Reread learning plans to find the key functions.</li>
  <li>Redo a few independent exercises to vary contexts and datasets.</li>
  <li>Practise rendering a complete Quarto document.</li>
  <li>Check your graphs: titles, axes, legends, units and interpretation.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Material and autonomy">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Personal resources</h3><p>Useful notes, challenges, adventures, solutions and code excerpts help you search quickly.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Without relying on the web</h3><p>Preparation should make you able to work with local resources and your understanding.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Goal</h3><p>Show a clear process, not only a numerical result.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="exam-day-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="exam-day-title">During the exam</h2>
  <p>The most robust strategy is to build a simple version that works, then improve it.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>Read the whole mission before coding.</li>
  <li>Import the data and check the structure with short outputs.</li>
  <li>Create the minimal transformations needed to answer the questions.</li>
  <li>Produce the requested graphs or tables.</li>
  <li>Render the document and fix errors before refining the writing.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Exam reflexes">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Name clearly</h3><p>Simple object names help reread code and find errors.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Test often</h3><p>Running chunks progressively avoids discovering every error at the final render.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Write briefly</h3><p>One precise sentence that answers the question is better than a vague paragraph.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="exam-check-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="exam-check-title">Final check</h2>
  <p>Before submitting, run a short and systematic check. It prevents most avoidable point losses.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>The Quarto document renders without error.</li>
  <li>The data used are imported by the document code.</li>
  <li>Each question has a visible answer.</li>
  <li>Graphs and tables have a title or clear context.</li>
  <li>Interpretations answer the mission rather than an R function.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Final reflexes">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Final render</h3><p>Open the rendered file, not only the source file.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Created objects</h3><p>Check that the document works in a fresh session.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Short text</h3><p>Add one precise sentence when the result alone is not enough.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <div class="resource-hub-grid">
  <article class="resource-hub-card">
  <h3>Fall 2025 - UN mission</h3>
  <p>Read these corrections before using the 2025 archive. Its exam-day rules do not define the 2026 rules. The CSV imports categories as text: create factors explicitly. The meaning and units of <code>gdp</code> are not reliably documented in the supplied file, so do not interpret it as GDP per capita or make economic claims from it. The Internet category is repeated unchanged across years for each country; it must not be used to infer historical Internet trends. Use the archive for technical practice, and prioritize the course adventures and exercises for substantive interpretation.</p>
  <p>For question 5, use <code>aes(x = gdp)</code> with <code>scale_x_log10()</code> to practise a log scale, without also computing <code>log(gdp)</code>. Document missing values, restrict the plot to positive available values, and use explicit shapes for the ordered Internet categories. The archive does not by itself cover all module 4 cleaning skills.</p>
  <p>A complete example of an applied exam: narrative context, dataset and guided questions on modules 1 to 4.</p>
